sanskrit: pañcabhir droṇaputras tu svayaṃ droṇaś ca saptabhiḥ śalyaś ca navabhir bāṇais tribhir duḥśāsanas tathā
english: Droṇa's son struck him with five arrows, and Droṇa himself with seven; Śalya with nine shafts, and Duḥśāsana likewise with three.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca viṃśatyā śakuniś cāpi pañcabhiḥ pāñcālyaṃ tvaritāvidhyan sarva eva mahārathāḥ
english: Duryodhana with twenty, and Śakuni too with five — all those great chariot-warriors swiftly pierced the prince of the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: sa viddhaḥ saptabhir vīrair droṇatrāṇārtham āhave sarvān asaṃbhramād rājan pratyavidhyat tribhis tribhiḥ droṇaṃ drauṇiṃ ca karṇaṃ ca vivyādha tava cātmajam
english: Wounded by those seven heroes who fought in battle to shield Droṇa, he, O king, without dismay struck back at each one with three arrows apiece, and pierced Droṇa, Droṇa's son, Karṇa, and your own son.

sanskrit: te viddhvā dhanvinā tena dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ punar mṛdhe vivyadhuḥ pañcabhis tūrṇam ekaiko rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Pierced by that bowman, those best of charioteers each in turn swiftly wounded Dhṛṣṭadyumna again in the fray, each with five shafts.

sanskrit: drumasenas tu saṃkruddho rājan vivyādha patriṇā tribhiś cānyaiḥ śarais tūrṇaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: But Drumasena, enraged, O king, pierced him with a feathered shaft and swiftly with three other arrows, crying, 'Stand! Stand!'

sanskrit: sa tu taṃ prativivyādha tribhis tīkṣṇair ajihmagaiḥ svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilādhautaiḥ prāṇāntakaraṇair yudhi
english: But he pierced him in return with three keen, straight-flying arrows, gold-feathered and whetted on stone, deadly bringers of death in battle.

sanskrit: bhallenānyena tu punaḥ suvarṇojjvalakuṇḍalam unmamātha śiraḥ kāyād drumasenasya vīryavān
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft the valiant one struck from its body the head of Drumasena, bright with golden earrings.

sanskrit: tacchiro nyapatad bhūmau saṃdaṣṭauṣṭhapuṭaṃ raṇe mahāvātasamuddhūtaṃ pakvaṃ tālaphalaṃ yathā
english: That head fell to the earth in the battle, its lips bitten fast together, like a ripe palm-fruit shaken loose by a mighty wind.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca viddhvā punar vīrān vīraḥ suniśitaiḥ śaraiḥ rādheyasyācchinad bhallaiḥ kārmukaṃ citrayodhinaḥ
english: And having pierced those heroes again with well-sharpened arrows, the hero with broad-headed shafts cut apart the bow of Rādheya, that artful fighter.

sanskrit: na tu tan mamṛṣe karṇo dhanuṣaś chedanaṃ tathā nikartanam ivātyugro lāṅgūlasya yathā hariḥ
english: But Karṇa could not endure that severing of his bow — fierce beyond measure, like a lion whose tail has been cut off.

sanskrit: so 'nyad dhanuḥ samādāya krodharaktekṣaṇaḥ śvasan abhyavarṣac charaughais taṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ mahābalam
english: Taking up another bow, his eyes red with rage and breathing hard, he rained floods of arrows upon that mighty Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu karṇaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ te vīrāḥ ṣaḍ ratharṣabhāḥ pāñcālyaputraṃ tvaritāḥ parivavrur jighāṃsayā
english: Seeing Karṇa thus enraged, those six bull-like chariot-warriors swiftly surrounded the son of the Pāñcāla king, eager to slay him.

sanskrit: ṣaṇṇāṃ yodhapravīrāṇāṃ tāvakānāṃ puraskṛtam mṛtyor āsyam anuprāptaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnam amaṃsmahi
english: Beset before those six foremost warriors of your side, Dhṛṣṭadyumna seemed to us to have come into the very mouth of death.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu dāśārho vikirañ śarān dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ parākrāntaṃ sātyakiḥ pratyapadyata
english: At that very moment the Dāśārha Sātyaki, scattering his arrows, came to the aid of the valiant Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: tam āyāntaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ sātyakiṃ yuddhadurmadam rādheyo daśabhir bāṇaiḥ pratyavidhyad ajihmagaiḥ
english: As that great archer Sātyaki, fierce in battle, drew near, Rādheya pierced him in return with ten straight-flying arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ sātyakir mahārāja vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ paśyatāṃ sarvavīrāṇāṃ mā gās tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Sātyaki, O great king, pierced him in turn with ten arrows before the eyes of all the heroes, crying, 'You shall not escape! Stand!'

sanskrit: sa sātyakes tu balinaḥ karṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ āsīt samāgamo ghoro balivāsavayor iva
english: Then between the mighty Sātyaki and the great-souled Karṇa there came a dreadful encounter, like that between Bali and Vāsava.

sanskrit: trāsayaṃs talaghoṣeṇa kṣatriyān kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ rājīvalocanaṃ karṇaṃ sātyakiḥ pratyavidhyata
english: That bull among kṣatriyas, terrifying the warriors with the slap of his palm against the bowstring, Sātyaki struck back at the lotus-eyed Karṇa.

sanskrit: kampayann iva ghoṣeṇa dhanuṣo vasudhāṃ balī sūtaputro mahārāja sātyakiṃ pratyayodhayat
english: The mighty son of the charioteer, as if making the earth tremble with the twang of his bow, fought back against Sātyaki, O great king.

sanskrit: vipāṭhakarṇinārācair vatsadantaiḥ kṣurair api karṇaḥ śaraśataiś cāpi śaineyaṃ pratyavidhyata
english: With cleaving shafts, with eared and iron arrows, with calf-tooth heads and razor-edged points, with hundreds of arrows besides, Karṇa pierced the grandson of Śini.

sanskrit: tathaiva yuyudhāno 'pi vṛṣṇīnāṃ pravaro rathaḥ abhyavarṣac charaiḥ karṇaṃ tad yuddham abhavat samam
english: And likewise Yuyudhāna too, foremost chariot-warrior of the Vṛṣṇis, rained arrows upon Karṇa; and that combat was evenly matched.

sanskrit: tāvakāś ca mahārāja karṇaputraś ca daṃśitaḥ sātyakiṃ vivyadhus tūrṇaṃ samantān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And your warriors, O great king, together with Karṇa's mailed son, swiftly pierced Sātyaki on every side with sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya teṣāṃ karṇasya cābhibho avidhyat sātyakiḥ kruddho vṛṣasenaṃ stanāntare
english: Warding off the weapons of those men and of Karṇa with his own weapons, O lord, the enraged Sātyaki struck Vṛṣasena in the breast.

sanskrit: tena bāṇena nirviddho vṛṣaseno viśāṃ pate nyapatat sa rathe mūḍho dhanur utsṛjya vīryavān
english: Pierced through by that arrow, O lord of peoples, the valiant Vṛṣasena, swooning, let fall his bow and sank down upon his chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo hataṃ matvā vṛṣasenaṃ mahārathaḥ putraśokābhisaṃtaptaḥ sātyakiṃ pratyapīḍayat
english: Then Karṇa, that great chariot-warrior, believing Vṛṣasena slain and burning with grief for his son, pressed hard upon Sātyaki in return.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānas tu karṇena yuyudhāno mahārathaḥ vivyādha bahubhiḥ karṇaṃ tvaramāṇaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Though hard pressed by Karṇa, the great chariot-warrior Yuyudhāna pierced Karṇa with many arrows, hastening again and again.

sanskrit: sa karṇaṃ daśabhir viddhvā vṛṣasenaṃ ca saptabhiḥ sahastāvāpadhanuṣī tayoś ciccheda sātvataḥ
english: Having pierced Karṇa with ten arrows and Vṛṣasena with seven, the Sātvata cut apart the bows of them both together with the guards upon their hands.

sanskrit: tāv anye dhanuṣī sajye kṛtvā śatrubhayaṃkare yuyudhānam avidhyetāṃ samantān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then those two, stringing other bows that struck terror into foes, pierced Yuyudhāna on every side with sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: vartamāne tu saṃgrāme tasmin vīravarakṣaye atīva śuśruve rājan gāṇḍīvasya mahāsvanaḥ
english: While that battle raged on, with its slaughter of the noblest heroes, the great twang of the Gāṇḍīva was heard above all, O king.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu rathanirghoṣaṃ gāṇḍīvasya ca nisvanam sūtaputro 'bravīd rājan duryodhanam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Hearing the rumble of the chariot and the twang of the Gāṇḍīva, the son of the charioteer, O king, spoke these words to Duryodhana.

sanskrit: eṣa sarvāñ śibīn hatvā mukhyaśaś ca nararṣabhān pauravāṃś ca maheṣvāsān gāṇḍīvaninado mahān
english: This mighty roar of the Gāṇḍīva comes from him who has slain all the Śibis, the foremost of men, and the great-bowed Pauravas.

sanskrit: śrūyate rathaghoṣaś ca vāsavasyeva nardataḥ karoti pāṇḍavo vyaktaṃ karmaupayikam ātmanaḥ
english: The din of his chariot is heard like the roar of Vāsava himself; plainly the Pāṇḍava is performing a deed worthy of his name.

sanskrit: eṣā vidīryate rājan bahudhā bhāratī camūḥ viprakīrṇāny anīkāni nāvatiṣṭhanti karhi cit
english: This Bhārata host, O king, is being torn asunder in many directions; the scattered ranks can hold their ground nowhere at all.

sanskrit: vāteneva samuddhūtam abhrajālaṃ vidīryate savyasācinam āsādya bhinnā naur iva sāgare
english: Like a mass of clouds scattered by the wind it is torn apart, having met Savyasācin, like a broken ship upon the sea.

sanskrit: dravatāṃ yodhamukhyānāṃ gāṇḍīvapreṣitaiḥ śaraiḥ viddhānāṃ śataśo rājañ śrūyate ninado mahān niśīthe rājaśārdūla stanayitnor ivāmbare
english: From the foremost warriors fleeing, pierced by the hundreds with arrows loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, a great cry is heard, O king — at midnight, O tiger among kings, like thunder in the sky.

sanskrit: hāhākāraravāṃś caiva siṃhanādāṃś ca puṣkalān śṛṇu śabdān bahuvidhān arjunasya rathaṃ prati
english: Hear the cries of dismay, the abundant lion-roars, and the sounds of many kinds rising up about the chariot of Arjuna.

sanskrit: ayaṃ madhye sthito 'smākaṃ sātyakiḥ sātvatādhamaḥ iha cel labhyate lakṣyaṃ kṛtsnāñ jeṣyāmahe parān
english: Here in our midst stands Sātyaki, the basest of the Sātvatas; if he be brought within our reach as a target here, we shall conquer all our foes.

sanskrit: eṣa pāñcālarājasya putro droṇena saṃgataḥ sarvataḥ saṃvṛto yodhai rājan puruṣasattamaiḥ
english: And here the son of the Pāñcāla king is locked with Droṇa, surrounded on every side, O king, by the noblest of warriors.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ yadi hanyāmo dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam asaṃśayaṃ mahārāja dhruvo no vijayo bhavet
english: If we should slay Sātyaki and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata, then beyond doubt, O great king, our victory would be assured.

sanskrit: saubhadravad imau vīrau parivārya mahārathau prayatāmo mahārāja nihantuṃ vṛṣṇipārṣatau
english: As we did with the son of Subhadrā, let us surround these two heroes, these great chariot-warriors, and strive, O great king, to slay the Vṛṣṇi and the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: savyasācī puro 'bhyeti droṇānīkāya bhārata saṃsaktaṃ sātyakiṃ jñātvā bahubhiḥ kurupuṃgavaiḥ
english: Savyasācin advances against Droṇa's army in front, O Bhārata, knowing that Sātyaki is locked in combat with many bulls among the Kurus.

sanskrit: tatra gacchantu bahavaḥ pravarā rathasattamāḥ yāvat pārtho na jānāti sātyakiṃ bahubhir vṛtam
english: Let many of our foremost, best of chariot-warriors go there, before Pārtha learns that Sātyaki is beset by many.

sanskrit: te tvaradhvaṃ yathā śūrāḥ śarāṇāṃ mokṣaṇe bhṛśam yathā tūrṇaṃ vrajaty eṣa paralokāya mādhavaḥ
english: Hasten, O heroes, eagerly in the loosing of your arrows, so that this Mādhava may swiftly pass to the world beyond.

sanskrit: karṇasya matam ājñāya putras te prāha saubalam yathendraḥ samare rājan prāha viṣṇuṃ yaśasvinam
english: Having learned Karṇa's counsel, your son spoke to the son of Subala, as Indra in battle, O king, once spoke to the glorious Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ sahasrair daśabhir gajānām anivartinām rathaiś ca daśasāhasrair vṛto yāhi dhanaṃjayam
english: 'Surrounded by ten thousand elephants that never turn back, and ringed by ten thousand chariots, go against Dhanaṃjaya.'

sanskrit: duḥśāsano durviṣahaḥ subāhur duṣpradharṣaṇaḥ ete tvām anuyāsyanti pattibhir bahubhir vṛtāḥ
english: 'Duḥśāsana, Durviṣaha, Subāhu, and Duṣpradharṣaṇa — these shall follow you, encircled by many footmen.'

sanskrit: jahi kṛṣṇau mahābāho dharmarājaṃ ca mātula nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca bhīmasenaṃ ca bhārata
english: 'Slay the two Kṛṣṇas, O mighty-armed uncle, and the Dharma-king too, and Nakula and Sahadeva and Bhīmasena, O Bhārata.'

sanskrit: devānām iva devendre jayāśā me tvayi sthitā jahi mātula kaunteyān asurān iva pāvakiḥ
english: 'As the gods place their hope of victory in the lord of the gods, so does my hope rest upon you. Slay, O uncle, the sons of Kuntī, as the son of Agni slew the Asuras.'

sanskrit: evam ukto yayau pārthān putreṇa tava saubalaḥ mahatyā senayā sārdhaṃ tava putrais tathā vibho
english: Thus addressed by your son, the son of Subala marched against the Pārthas with a great army and with your sons as well, O lord.

sanskrit: priyārthaṃ tava putrāṇāṃ didhakṣuḥ pāṇḍunandanān tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tāvakānāṃ paraiḥ saha
english: To please your sons, longing to consume the joy-bringing sons of Pāṇḍu, then arose the battle between your men and the foe.

sanskrit: prayāte saubale rājan pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm balena mahatā yuktaḥ sūtaputras tu sātvatam
english: When the son of Subala had marched against the host of the Pāṇḍavas, O king, the son of the charioteer, joined with a great force, advanced against the Sātvata.

sanskrit: abhyayāt tvaritaṃ yuddhe kirañ śaraśatān bahūn tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ sarve sātyakiṃ paryavārayan
english: He charged swiftly into the fight, scattering many hundreds of arrows; and likewise all the Pāṇḍavas closed protectively around Sātyaki.

sanskrit: mahad yuddhaṃ tadāsīt tu droṇasya niśi bhārata dhṛṣṭadyumnena śūreṇa pāñcālaiś ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Then a great battle was fought by night, O Bhārata, between Droṇa on the one side and the heroic Dhṛṣṭadyumna with the great-souled Pāñcālas on the other.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatas te prādravan sarve tvaritā yuddhadurmadāḥ amṛṣyamāṇāḥ saṃrabdhā yuyudhānarathaṃ prati
english: Saṃjaya said: Then they all rushed forward in haste, frenzied in battle, unable to bear it and filled with fury, toward the chariot of Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: te rathaiḥ kalpitai rājan hemarūpyavibhūṣitaiḥ sādibhiś ca gajaiś caiva parivavruḥ sma sātvatam
english: With their well-equipped chariots adorned with gold and silver, O king, and with horsemen and elephants, they surrounded the Sātvata.

sanskrit: athainaṃ koṣṭhakīkṛtya sarvatas te mahārathāḥ siṃhanādāṃs tadā cakrus tarjayantaḥ sma sātyakim
english: Then, hemming him in on every side as in a stockade, those great chariot-warriors raised their lion-roars, threatening Sātyaki.

sanskrit: te 'bhyavarṣañ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ sātyakiṃ satyavikramam tvaramāṇā mahāvīryā mādhavasya vadhaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Those mighty heroes, hastening and seeking the death of the Mādhava, rained sharp arrows upon Sātyaki of true valor.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā patatas tūrṇaṃ śaineyaḥ paravīrahā pratyagṛhṇān mahābāhuḥ pramuñcan viśikhān bahūn
english: Seeing them swiftly descending upon him, the grandson of Śini, slayer of hostile heroes, that mighty-armed one received them, loosing many arrows in return.

sanskrit: tatra vīro maheṣvāsaḥ sātyakir yuddhadurmadaḥ nicakarta śirāṃsy ugraiḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: There the hero Sātyaki, great archer fierce in battle, cut off heads with terrible arrows whose joints were bent low.

sanskrit: hastihastān hayagrīvān bāhūn api ca sāyudhān kṣurapraiḥ pātayām āsa tāvakānāṃ sa mādhavaḥ
english: The trunks of elephants, the necks of horses, and arms still grasping their weapons — these the Mādhava brought down with razor-headed shafts among your men.

sanskrit: patitaiś cāmaraiś caiva śvetacchatraiś ca bhārata babhūva dharaṇī pūrṇā nakṣatrair dyaur iva prabho
english: With fallen yak-tail whisks and white parasols, O Bhārata, the earth became filled, like the sky with stars, O lord.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu yuyudhānena yudhyatāṃ yudhi bhārata babhūva tumulaḥ śabdaḥ pretānām iva krandatām
english: As they battled with Yuyudhāna in the fray, O Bhārata, there arose a tumultuous din, like the wailing of departed spirits.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā pūritāsīd vasuṃdharā rātriḥ samabhavac caiva tīvrarūpā bhayāvahā
english: By that mighty sound the earth was filled, and the night became fierce of aspect and terrifying.

sanskrit: dīryamāṇaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā yuyudhānaśarāhatam śrutvā ca vipulaṃ nādaṃ niśīthe lomaharṣaṇam
english: Seeing the army torn apart and struck down by Yuyudhāna's arrows, and hearing the vast hair-raising clamor at midnight,

sanskrit: sutas tavābravīd rājan sārathiṃ rathināṃ varaḥ yatraiṣa śabdas tatrāśvāṃś codayeti punaḥ punaḥ
english: your son, that best of chariot-warriors, O king, said again and again to his charioteer, 'Drive the horses to where this sound arises.'

sanskrit: tena saṃcodyamānas tu tatas tāṃs turagottamān sūtaḥ saṃcodayām āsa yuyudhānarathaṃ prati
english: Thus urged on, the charioteer then drove those excellent horses toward the chariot of Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ kruddho dṛḍhadhanvā jitaklamaḥ śīghrahastaś citrayodhī yuyudhānam upādravat
english: Then Duryodhana, enraged, firm of bow, untiring, swift of hand, and skilled in varied modes of warfare, rushed upon Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair māṃsaśoṇitabhojanaiḥ duryodhanaṃ dvādaśabhir mādhavaḥ pratyavidhyata
english: Then with arrows loosed from a fully drawn bow, feeders on flesh and blood, the Mādhava pierced Duryodhana in return with twelve shafts.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tena tathā pūrvam evārditaḥ śaraiḥ śaineyaṃ daśabhir bāṇaiḥ pratyavidhyad amarṣitaḥ
english: Duryodhana, thus already wounded before by those arrows, pierced the grandson of Śini in return with ten shafts, unable to bear it.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddham ākulaṃ bharatarṣabha pāñcālānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ bhāratānāṃ ca dāruṇam
english: Then there arose a confused and terrible battle, O bull of the Bhāratas, between all the Pāñcālas and the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: śaineyas tu raṇe kruddhas tava putraṃ mahāratham sāyakānām aśītyā tu vivyādhorasi bhārata
english: The grandson of Śini, enraged in the fight, pierced your son, that great chariot-warrior, in the breast with eighty arrows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato 'sya vāhān samare śarair ninye yamakṣayam sārathiṃ ca rathāt tūrṇaṃ pātayām āsa patriṇā
english: Then in the battle he sent his horses with arrows to the abode of Yama, and swiftly with a feathered shaft brought down his charioteer from the car.

sanskrit: hatāśve tu rathe tiṣṭhan putras tava viśāṃ pate mumoca niśitān bāṇāñ śaineyasya rathaṃ prati
english: Standing upon his car whose horses were slain, your son, O lord of peoples, loosed sharpened arrows toward the chariot of the grandson of Śini.

sanskrit: śarān pañcāśatas tāṃs tu śaineyaḥ kṛtahastavat ciccheda samare rājan preṣitāṃs tanayena te
english: Those fifty arrows sent forth by your son, O king, the grandson of Śini, deft of hand, cut to pieces in the battle.

sanskrit: athāpareṇa bhallena muṣṭideśe mahad dhanuḥ ciccheda rabhaso yuddhe tava putrasya māriṣa
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft the impetuous one, in the fight, cut your son's great bow at the grip, O honored sir.

sanskrit: viratho vidhanuṣkaś ca sarvalokeśvaraḥ prabhuḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ bhāsvaraṃ kṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: Bereft of his chariot and of his bow, that lord and master of all the world swiftly mounted the gleaming car of Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: duryodhane parāvṛtte śaineyas tava vāhinīm drāvayām āsa viśikhair niśāmadhye viśāṃ pate
english: When Duryodhana had turned away, the grandson of Śini put your army to flight with his arrows in the dead of night, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: śakuniś cārjunaṃ rājan parivārya samantataḥ rathair anekasāhasrair gajaiś caiva sahasraśaḥ tathā hayasahasraiś ca tumulaṃ sarvato 'karot
english: And Śakuni, O king, surrounding Arjuna on every side with many thousands of chariots, with elephants by the thousand, and with thousands of horses, raised a tumult all around.

sanskrit: te mahāstrāṇi divyāni vikiranto 'rjunaṃ prati arjunaṃ yodhayanti sma kṣatriyāḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: Scattering great celestial weapons against Arjuna, those kṣatriyas, driven on by fate, did battle with Arjuna.

sanskrit: tāny arjunaḥ sahasrāṇi rathavāraṇavājinām pratyavārayad āyastaḥ prakurvan vipulaṃ kṣayam
english: Those thousands of chariots, elephants, and horses Arjuna held back, exerting himself and working a vast destruction.
